To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the chiral and the deconfinement transitions are first order at the physical point, that the critical temperature is 154(3)MeV and that the equation of state is very soft at temperatures below the transition temperature.

we find a critical temperature of about 170(5)MeV in 2+1 flavors QCD with almost physical quark masses, and that the pressure in the high temperature phase is well described by a Stefan-Boltzmann formula.

(1) the quark mass dependence of the order parameter is consistent with a linear scaling law, (2) the quark number susceptibility shows a clear peak structure at a temperature of 170 MeV, (3) the static quark potential is consistent with a string picture at temperatures below 170 MeV and (4) the quark masses and the cut-off are consistent with the scaling law of a second order phase transition at a temperature of about 170 MeV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of the QCD equation of state for a wide range of temperatures and quark masses and the study of the quark and gluon degrees of freedom in hot and dense matter.
the thermodynamic properties of QCD in the vicinity of the deconfinement transition with almost realistic quarks masses.
the determination of thermodynamic properties in the low temperature regime of QCD with almost physical quark masses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the phase transition is a smooth crossover for the currently used quark masses and lattice spacings.

the QCD phase diagram is not very sensitive to the details of the quark masses, and that it is very likely that a first-order phase transition exists for quark masses below 1/3 of the physical value, as expected in the literature.
the critical temperature is not very sensitive to quark mass and lattice spacing variations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are now able to study QCD thermodynamics with almost realistic quarks masses and with the same lattice spacing as used in the simulations for the determination of the QCD vacuum properties.
we are able to determine thermodynamic quantities with almost realistic quarks masses and a cut-off of the order 500 MeV, which is the smallest cut-off used so far.
we have found a very strong cut-off dependence of the order parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cut-off dependence of the thermodynamics is much smaller than the quark mass dependence.
, in the chiral limit, the critical temperature and the equation of state can be extrapolated to the physical quark masses using chiral perturbation theory.
